newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania okays sale of gas firm shares - agency.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania okays sale of gas firm shares - agency.

text.p: The Lithuanian government on Wednesday approved plans for the country's state-owned gas company Lithuanian Gas to sell some of its shares to private investors as part of a capital increase, domestic news agency ELTA said.
It said the government backed a plan for the gas company to boost its share capital to 66 million litas.

The increase in capital and sale to private investors would cause the state's share in the gas firm to fall to 76.04 percent from 91.08 percent and private shareholdings to rise 5.04 percent to 23.96 percent, ELTA said.
The shares will be sold in a closed auction and the minimum price has been set at one litas, ELTA said.
It quoted Industry and Commerce Minister Kazimieras Klimashauskas as saying the sale of some shares to private investors was the only way to get more funds for the cash-strapped company.
A successful share sale would also show if investors were interested in the gas company, ELTA quoted the minister adding.
Lithuania's whole energy sector needs restructuring and the country has run up large debts to Russia, its supplier of gas.
ELTA said government plans called for investments of $558 million to modernise the gas sector within 20 years.
